$comment: VRFY-29 (D-20-19): Pass 3 acceptance corpus. Each row is a draft; tests/known-bad-quotes.test.ts finds its one quote with
extractQuotes and checks it with runPass3 against the source text below, served two ways: as the user's own hash-verified
PDF (a real PDF drawn from the text, re-hashed by byo-text.ts; no network) and as the Europe PMC open-access full text of
the work (JATS built from the text, answered by a local mock; the article names the citation's DOI).
Every PDF artifact class (ligature, soft hyphen, smart quotes, ellipsis, diacritic; plus the em dash) appears in the source
text and in claimed quotes. Every NOT_FOUND row must be NOT_FOUND on both routes; every PASS row must PASS on both.
The text is from Vaswani et al. 2017 (arXiv 1706.03762), shortened; the DOI and PMCID are test identifiers.
Rows past the artifact classes: whole-word edits (an inserted negator, a changed number or word) and elisions that stitch
distant passages or single words must be NOT_FOUND even when close by characters; an editorial [bracket] is not quoted text.
Review round 2: quotes in other languages' quotation marks (guillemets, low-high marks) and a Title Case quote after a reporting colon are extracted and checked like any other.

source.title: Attention Is All You Need
source.text:
Attention Is All You Need
The dominant sequence trans­duction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring signiﬁcantly less time to train.
Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output sequences … this inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples.
The encoder—a stack of six identical layers—maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations.
We call our particular attention “Scaled Dot-Product Attention” and compute the dot products of the query with all keys.
A naïve implementation of self-attention would be slower than recurrent layers for very long sequences.
To the best of our knowledge, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output.
On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model outperforms the best previously reported models by more than 2.0 BLEU.

quotes.claimed_quote: Attention is all you need to solve every NLP problem.
quotes.draft: The paper states that "Attention is all you need to solve every NLP problem." [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: Completely fabricated claim: the sentence does not appear in the paper.

quotes.claimed_quote: Our model achieves a BLEU score of 99.9 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task.
quotes.draft: In their words, “Our model achieves a BLEU score of 99.9 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task.” [@vaswani2017].
quotes.note: Fabricated BLEU score: the paper reports 28.4 for the big model.

quotes.claimed_quote: The Transformer is the ﬁrst sequence model to achieve state-of-the-art results without any recurrence.
quotes.draft: The paper states that "The Transformer is the ﬁrst sequence model to achieve state-of-the-art results without any recurrence." [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: U+FB01 in the claim; normalization handles it, and the wording is fabricated.

quotes.claimed_quote: The trans­former architecture eliminates recurrence entirely and relies solely on attention mechanisms.
quotes.draft: As @vaswani2017 [p. 4] put it, "The trans­former architecture eliminates recurrence entirely and relies solely on attention mechanisms."
quotes.note: U+00AD in the claim; normalization strips it, and the wording is fabricated.

quotes.claimed_quote: Queries, keys, and values are all mapped to an “attention space” where the similarity is computed.
quotes.draft: They write ‘Queries, keys, and values are all mapped to an “attention space” where the similarity is computed.’ [see @vaswani2017, p. 3].
quotes.note: U+201C/U+201D inside the claim; the phrase "attention space" is not in the paper.

quotes.claimed_quote: The model learns an end—to—end mapping from input sequences to output sequences.
quotes.draft: The paper states that "The model learns an end—to—end mapping from input sequences to output sequences." [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: U+2014 in the claim; the phrase does not appear.

quotes.claimed_quote: The naïve dot-product attention scales quadratically with sequence length.
quotes.draft:
The paper puts it this way.

> The naïve dot-product attention scales quadratically with sequence length.

[@vaswani2017, p. 5]
quotes.note: U+00EF in the claim; the sentence is fabricated (the paper has a different sentence with "naïve").

quotes.claimed_quote: Positional encodings are learned parameters that replace the need for recurrence.
quotes.draft: In their words, “Positional encodings are learned parameters that replace the need for recurrence.” [@vaswani2017].
quotes.note: Fabricated: the paper uses fixed sinusoidal encodings.

quotes.claimed_quote: Multi-head attention allows the model to simultaneously attend to all positions in the sequence with equal weight.
quotes.draft: The paper states that "Multi-head attention allows the model to simultaneously attend to all positions in the sequence with equal weight." [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: Fabricated "equal weight".

quotes.claimed_quote: The Transformer completely eliminates the need for language-specific preprocessing such as tokenization.
quotes.draft: As @vaswani2017 [p. 4] put it, "The Transformer completely eliminates the need for language-specific preprocessing such as tokenization."
quotes.note: Fabricated claim.

quotes.claimed_quote: Each decoder layer applies cross-attention over the entire encoder output in O(1) time complexity.
quotes.draft: The paper states that "Each decoder layer applies cross-attention over the entire encoder output in O(1) time complexity." [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: Fabricated complexity claim.

quotes.claimed_quote: The ﬁnal layer norm ensures that all hidden states have unit variance before projection.
quotes.draft: They write ‘The ﬁnal layer norm ensures that all hidden states have unit variance before projection.’ [see @vaswani2017, p. 3].
quotes.note: U+FB01 in the claim; fabricated.

quotes.claimed_quote: Recurrent models typically factor computation … and process every token in parallel across all training examples.
quotes.draft:
The paper puts it this way.

> Recurrent models typically factor computation … and process every token in parallel across all training examples.

[@vaswani2017, p. 5]
quotes.note: U+2026 in the claim: the first part is real, the part after the elision is not in the paper.

quotes.claimed_quote: The best performing penguins also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism.
quotes.draft: In their words, “The best performing penguins also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism.” [@vaswani2017].
quotes.note: One word changed ("models" → "penguins"): below the 0.95 threshold, never FUZZY.

quotes.claimed_quote: more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train
quotes.draft: The paper states that "more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train" [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: The source has U+FB01 ("signiﬁcantly"); the claim has plain "fi".

quotes.draft: As @vaswani2017 [p. 4] put it, "the Transformer is the ﬁrst transduction model relying entirely on self-attention"
quotes.note: The claim has U+FB01; the source has plain "first".

quotes.draft: In their words, “The dominant sequence transduction models … outperforms the best previously reported models by more than 2.0 BLEU.” [@vaswani2017].
quotes.note: Both parts are real, but they lie a whole abstract apart: an elision never stitches distant passages into one quotation.

quotes.claimed_quote: recurrent … attention … Transformer … parallelizable … BLEU
quotes.draft: The paper states that "recurrent … attention … Transformer … parallelizable … BLEU" [@vaswani2017].
quotes.note: Single words that each occur in the paper, in order, joined by elisions: fragments, not a quotation.

quotes.draft: They write ‘To the best of our knowledge, the Transformer is not the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output.’ [@vaswani2017, p. 2].
quotes.note: An inserted "not" inverts the sentence; at 97% character similarity it must still be refused (a whole word differs).

quotes.draft: In their words, “On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model outperforms the best previously reported models by more than 3.0 BLEU.” [@vaswani2017, p. 8].
quotes.note: One digit changed (2.0 to 3.0): a number in a quote must match exactly.
